topics.topic: Durable model effects permitted after failed delivery
questions: May a failed delivery create or change any durable model other than a placement, such as a rejection record or status, or must all model state remain unchanged?
Besides forbidding a placement, may a failed delivery create or change any model such as a rejection status, delivery-attempt record, diagnostic record or cached source observation?
Does failed delivery create or change any deliverable or failure model even though it creates no placement?

quotes:
The answer to one delivery. `source_id` is the one the caller requested. It holds the placement facts
when there is a placement, and the Portal `photo_id` when the photo is already marked as published.
- Continuity: An outcome belongs to one delivery and does not continue after it.

### Persistence candidate

Calculated on demand.
judgement.why: The only failed-delivery model is an on-demand value outcome with no continuity or persistence, while a durable PhotoPlacement exists only when placement succeeds.

questions: Which metadata facts cross the boundary and become model facts, and which model owns them?

quotes:
What one scan saw for one file of the photo folder. A placed file adds its `file_ref`, a published
file adds its Portal `photo_id`, and files with the same content carry the same `source_id`. The
deliverer computes it on each scan; the calling flow reads it. A server path is never part of it. `size`
is the size the file's metadata gave when it was listed.

The image made from a source file for the Portal: upright pixels only, at most 2000 px on the
longest side, with the moment the photo was taken as UTC without an offset, and how that moment
was obtained (P-03, P-05). It exists only while a placement is made.
**Fields:** `content: bytes`, `taken_at: datetime`, `date_source: DateSource`.
judgement.why: State 1 models listed size as scan-observation metadata and the selected time plus provenance as PreparedPhoto facts; other raw metadata remains input rather than model identity.

judgement.why: P16 already decides that scan observations have no continuity and that durable delivery identity is content-based rather than path-based.

precedent.topic: Stable identity of a source photo across observations
quotes: - Continuity: Nothing continues between scans; the next scan observes the folder again.
- Minted by: the deliverer, from `project_id` and `source_id`, the SHA-256 of the source content.
- Issued: a placement is a fact about one observed content and is never rewritten.
precedent.why: Source observations have no identity continuity across scans, while the durable placement identity is content-based within a project rather than path- or filesystem-identity-based.
